chunks: "I'll start with the input source on the left and draw a line out to the right. In series with that line I put the inductor. At the right end of the inductor is the switch node.
From there I draw the switch, a MOSFET, going down to ground, with its gate driven by a PWM signal.
Then, also from the switch node, I put a diode going to the right with the anode at the switch node and the cathode toward the output.
After the diode is the output node, with a capacitor to ground and then the load.
So the path is V in , inductor, switch node, diode, V out , and the switch hangs off the switch node to ground.
I'd label the switch node, mark the inductor current direction, and add a ground symbol.

If I have space I'd add the real-world bits: an input capacitor, a feedback divider from the output back to the controller, and I'd mention that in a synchronous version the diode gets replaced by a second MOSFET.
The easy check: the inductor goes on the input side, which is different from a buck where it's on the output side."
